question: persister
prompt:
Each of your ideas must draw on a domain unrelated to the research question below, for example through an analogy, a structure, a principle, or a pattern borrowed from that domain, while still being a concrete, scientifically sound way to address the question.

Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Flight-recorder molecular memory (aviation black boxes)
ideas.description: Use a CRISPR base-editor 'recorder' that writes signaling and transcription-factor activity (AP-1, NF-kB, ERK, Wnt) into genomic barcodes during the days before drug exposure. Then sequence the recordings in survivors versus matched untreated cells to identify which pre-existing states predicted survival.

ideas.title: Twin-study heritability of fate (human behavioral genetics)
ideas.description: Perform time-lapse imaging of full lineage trees with drug added at varied times post-division, measuring fate concordance between sisters, cousins, and more distant relatives. The decay of concordance with genealogical distance estimates how long a survival-priming state is heritable versus randomly reset.

ideas.title: Actuarial hazard modeling of single-cell death (life-insurance statistics)
ideas.description: Image cells carrying multiple live reporters (ERK kinase translocation, caspase sensor, FUCCI cell cycle, mitochondrial potential) through treatment. Fit time-varying-covariate survival models to find which dynamic features, not snapshot levels, shift a cell's instantaneous risk of death.

ideas.title: Early-warning signals of tipping points (ecology and climate science)
ideas.description: Test whether cells entering a drug-tolerant state show critical slowing down -- rising variance, autocorrelation, and flickering in reporter time series -- before committing. This would let you prospectively flag and sort pre-transition cells for molecular profiling.

ideas.title: Microenvironmental neighborhood effects (urban epidemiology)
ideas.description: Treat each cell's local context as a neighborhood exposure: use spatial transcriptomics or imaging of dense cultures and organoids to test whether survival clusters spatially. Regress survival on local density, neighbor identity, and diffusible-factor gradients to separate cell-intrinsic priming from niche-conferred protection.
